subject: Human Evolution
title: Persistence Hunting Today
description: A micro-lesson that makes Persistence Hunting Today usable.

hook.text: The San people of the Kalahari still chase kudu antelope on foot until the animal collapses from heat.

buildup.text: A hunt can last 4–5 hours over 25–35 km in searing midday heat—when most predators are resting.

discovery.text: The hunter tracks at a jog, never letting the animal rest long enough to cool down via panting.

twist.text: This technique requires no weapons—just legs, sweat, and the ability to track prints at speed.

climax.text: Persistence hunting is living proof that our ancestors ran down dinner before they invented spears.

punchline.text: The oldest hunt needs no weapon but patience.

quiz.question: How does persistence hunting work?
options: Chasing animals until they overheat and collapse
